reuse.why: Extends getDateWithSkippedWeekend and adds isHoliday/isNonWorkingDay, but the new server code spells out 'isWeekend || isHoliday' inline instead of calling its own isNonWorkingDay, and schedule-template.ts is not given holidays.

duplication.why: The daily-skip decision is written three times (getNextDate loop, getUpcomingDates flatMap, getDatesInRange flatMap), each with its own skipWeekend/daily branching around getDateWithSkippedWeekend.

placement.why: The day predicates sit in shared/schedules.ts, but how an occurrence is adjusted or dropped is decided separately in shared getNextDate and in two server handlers.

scope.why: Edits serve the four steps (including passing holidays through parseRecurDate), with no unrelated changes.

maintainability.why: Three diverging copies of the adjust-or-skip rule (one with a 366-step loop, holidays taken from dateCond.value or schedule.data) plus a template path that ignores holidays make future rule changes error-prone.

bypasses_abstraction.where: server/schedules/app.ts getUpcomingDates and getDatesInRange inline d.isWeekend || isHoliday instead of isNonWorkingDay and re-implement the daily skip; server/budget/schedule-template.ts calls getDateWithSkippedWeekend without holidays or daily skip

disguised_duplication.where: the adjust-or-skip-daily rule appears as a retry loop in getNextDate and as two differently shaped flatMaps (early-return order differs) in getUpcomingDates and getDatesInRange

abstraction_drift.where: getDateWithSkippedWeekend gains a holidays parameter; getNextDate gains isDaily branches (skip loop, early null return, exclusion from the shared move); getUpcomingDates, getDatesInRange and schedule-template.ts bypass or re-implement the rule
